rationale: Power intent is per-implementation, not protocol-level

extraction_strategy.ic_class_applicability_gate_v0_1_62: ic_class='serial_peripheral_protocol' declares LL21 not applicable; emitted as N/A stub (l_doc_taxonomy.na_stub)

low_power_modes_summary.Power_Down: PHY analog OFF (mostly); MDIO responsive; ≤ 0.5 s exit.
low_power_modes_summary.Isolate: MII / GMII drivers high-Z; PHY still consumes baseline + analog standby; MDIO responsive.
low_power_modes_summary.EEE_LPI: (Post-2005) Per-direction LPI signaling; PHY analog enters low-power; quick wake on traffic-pending.

fields.notes: IEEE Std 802.3-2005 specifies a minimal but mandatory power-management surface in BMCR (Reset / Loopback / Power Down / Isolate). Energy Efficient Ethernet (Clause 78, added in IEEE 802.3az-2010) extended this with the LPI signalling that lets the PHY analog enter a deeper sleep when the MAC has no traffic, and Clause 22 + 45 management registers were extended to control + observe the EEE state machine. Wake-on-LAN is an industry feature not part of the IEEE 802.3 standard but widely supported across NICs and integrated PHYs.
fields.ieee_1149_4_optional_extension: IEEE Std 1149.4 (Mixed-Signal Test Bus) adds analog test-pin observability layered on the 1149.1 TAP; it includes some power-related instructions but is a separate standard.

link_power_management_states.description: MAC + PHY both running; AutoNeg complete; link up; normal frame TX + RX in progress.

PHY in low-power state. MDIO bus remains responsive (PHY still answers C22 / C45 register accesses). PHY shall NOT generate spurious MII / GMII activity. RX_CLK / TX_CLK signal-quality requirements are relaxed.
link_power_management_states.exit_latency_estimate: ≤ 0.5 s after both BMCR 0.11 and 0.10 are cleared

link_power_management_states.description: PHY data paths to MII / GMII are high-Z (TX_CLK, RX_CLK, RX_DV, RX_ER, RXD, COL, CRS); PHY ignores TXD / TX_EN / TX_ER / GTX_CLK; MDIO still responsive. Used for multi-PHY hot-insertion and board test.
PHY reset in progress; BMCR + BMSR restored to defaults; PHY is unresponsive to writes other than 0.15 itself. Self-clearing.
Energy Efficient Ethernet Low-Power Idle. When MAC has no traffic, PHY transmits LPI symbols (refresh + sleep + quiet); receiver wakes on a refresh tone. Reduces PHY analog power during idle periods.
link_power_management_states.exit_latency_estimate: 10-20 µs (TX_LPI_WAKE_TIMER) for 100BASE-TX; longer for 1000BASE-T (16.5 µs); much longer for 10GBASE-T (~5 µs typical + alignment)

device_states_d0_d3_analog.description: BMCR.Power Down = 0 and Isolate = 0. PHY analog + digital fully on. Equivalent to ACPI D0.
BMCR.Isolate = 1. Equivalent to D2 — PHY logic on, MII drivers off.
BMCR.Power Down = 1. Most PHY analog gated off. MDIO responsive. Equivalent to D3hot.
RESET# asserted. All PHY logic in reset. Equivalent to D3cold.

auxiliary_power_for_wake_on_lan.Vaux_support: Implementation-defined. Many PHYs accept a separate Vaux rail so they can stay alive in D3cold and emit a Magic Packet wake-up event to the host (Wake-on-LAN).
auxiliary_power_for_wake_on_lan.Vaux_usage_hint: Required for any deployment that must wake the system on receipt of a designated frame (Magic Packet) while main power is off.

pause_flow_control_summary.PAUSE_direction: Per-direction (one or both); IEEE 802.3x specifies symmetric PAUSE only; Asymmetric PAUSE (PFC) requires negotiation per Annex 28B.

fields.power_considerations: Low-speed open-drain signaling with an external pull-up; static power dominated by the pull-up when MDIO is driven low.
